teams.heading: Steve Hansen says Mark Nawaqanitawase would be better off playing for Fiji
teams.body: Former All Blacks coach Sir Steve Hansen has said Mark Nawaqanitawase "would be better off playing for Fiji", given his commitments to Japanese club the Saitama Wild Knights. The 26-year-old, who won 11 Australia caps before two years in rugby league with the Sydney Roosters, is still weighing his Test options and is also eligible for Italy and Fiji. Speaking on the Rugby Unity podcast, Hansen said he hopes the wing still plays for Australia. Nawaqanitawase is not in Jake White's 35-man squad.

lead.why: Items 1 and 2 are Rugby League World Cup coverage, item 4 was already reported today, and item 3 offers only a headline, so this is the strongest men's 15s story with a sourced body.

teams.heading: Club rugby: Ollie Chessum pinches Bristol lineouts as Leicester win 22-16
teams.body: In Premiership club rugby, Leicester Tigers beat Bristol Bears 22-16 at Ashton Gate on Friday night, going top of the table for now. England hopeful Ollie Chessum was the clear player of the match, with Leicester winning 94 per cent of their own lineout ball to Bristol's 71 per cent. Billy Searle's boot did much of the damage, with three of Leicester's four tries coming off it, two while Bristol were a man short.

teams.heading: Tadhg Furlong cleared to play after disciplinary hearing over Gavin Coombes citation
teams.body: Tadhg Furlong has been cleared to play after his disciplinary hearing over the Gavin Coombes citation. Munster have issued a statement on the outcome and will give Coombes full backing. Ireland's next match is against Argentina, whose 33-man Nations Championship roster, finalised this week, brings back veteran Facundo Isa after missing out on international duty in 2024 and 2026.

teams.heading: Quesada says Italy captaincy decision comes next week with 17 players injured
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada has said Italy will name their captain next week, with 17 players unavailable through injury. Speaking at the launch of the Northern Phase, he said the team has some ideas, pointing to players who have captained before, such as Giacomo Nicotera and Niccolò Cannone, and to others for whom it could be a new opportunity. The choice will depend on the group and who is available. Italy face South Africa in Turin, then Argentina in Genoa and Fiji in Udine before London.

teams.heading: Jack Singleton scores on Glasgow debut after cardiac event; Warriors beat Lions
teams.body: Jack Singleton marked his Glasgow debut with a try in the 35th minute as the Warriors beat the Lions 28-20 at Scotstoun, keeping their unbeaten run alive. The 30-year-old, a former England hooker, had a cardiac event during training at Gloucester last year and had stents and balloons fitted, and this was his first appearance in 13 months. Fergus Watson opened the scoring as the Warriors led 19-3 at half-time, before the Lions fought back in the second half.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item in the pack and the only one with a concrete on-pitch event, a debut and comeback, rather than an interview or schedule piece.

teams.heading: Wales wing Ellis Mee signs new Scarlets contract, length undisclosed
teams.body: Ellis Mee has committed his future to Scarlets with a new contract, though the length of the deal has not been disclosed. The 23-year-old has made 43 appearances for the region since arriving from Nottingham in 2024, scoring 11 tries, and has 11 Test caps for Wales since his debut against Ireland in the 2025 Six Nations. Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies called him an exciting player and a great character within the group. Mee is in Steve Tandy's squad for the Nations Championship games.

teams.heading: Galindo names Bernasconi-led Argentina XV to face England A in Bath
teams.body: Álvaro Galindo has named his 27-man Argentina XV for the uncapped match against England A in Bath, headlined by Benetton hooker Bernardo Bernasconi. Harlequins prop Pedro Delgado and Bristol Bears flanker Benjamín Grondona are in the group, both among the players missing from Felipe Contepomi's Los Pumas roster. The XV trained for four days at Hindú Club in Buenos Aires, and the fixture gives players from both sides a chance at call-ups to the test arena.

lead.why: The Isa recall is already covered, and this is the strongest new item: a fresh Argentina XV squad with a headline hooker and two missing Pumas.

teams.heading: Angus Crichton signs with Waratahs for 2027, switching from NRL to union
teams.body: Angus Crichton, the Kangaroos and Blues Origin star, signed with the NSW Waratahs for 2027 back in January, a late switch from the NRL ahead of next year's home World Cup. The 29-year-old, who grew up playing union and came close to joining the Western Force after the 2023 World Cup, joins former Roosters teammate Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii at the Tahs, with a get-out clause after the 2027 World Cup. "It's incredibly exciting to be returning to the sport I played throughout my childhood," Crichton said.

teams.heading: Japan's best-ever world ranking is No. 7, set in 2019
teams.body: Japan's peak in the world rankings is No. 7, reached in 2019. In the Nations Championship so far, Japan have won one of three matches, losing two. Across those three, they have scored 62 points and conceded 88, a points difference of -26. Their most recent result was a 28-34 defeat to Fiji. Wales are the next opponent, in Round 4 of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Sir John Kirwan urges Rennie to use Ma'u and Tosi's size
teams.body: Sir John Kirwan, speaking on the Rivals podcast, wants the All Blacks to play more size up front, especially against South Africa. Saula Ma'u and Pasilio Tosi are both around 22st, and Ma'u came into the 36-man squad after Tyrel Lomax was ruled out with a neck issue. Kirwan conceded they may not yet be the best in their position, but said: "I do think we need their size." Ma'u, who has yet to earn a cap, impressed in the tour game against the Lions.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus posts cryptic voice note after Tadhg Furlong is cleared
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has posted a cryptic voice note on social media, appearing to comment on Leinster and Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong being cleared of allegedly grabbing Munster No. 8 Gavin Coombes' testicles during a URC match last week. The voice note's caption read "The saddest is everyone know this was going to happen." In contrast, Bulls and Bok hooker Jan-Hendrik Wessels was suspended for nine weeks, later reduced to eight, over allegedly grabbing Connacht flank Josh Murphy's testicles last season, despite no clear video evidence.

lead.why: It is a new item about the Springbok coach himself, and it is the one a fan would text a mate about, unlike the already-reported squad and selection stories.
